content.comment_body: Are there any [product_name] or [product_name] logs generated during the cloud download process that are accessible for review?

Just a quick update for everyone: with the assistance of [company_name] support teams in several regions, we identified the reason why my [product_name] application was not functioning properly after downloading it to AWS cloud. The issue stemmed from downloading AWS Access Keys as a .csv file. The cells for both Access Key and Secret Access Key included an extra space at the end of the string, which should be removed. When copying and pasting these values into the [product_name] setup, the additional space is included, potentially causing the application to not work as expected once in AWS cloud. Since [product_name] does not currently provide an error message for this, users might be unsure why the setup isn’t working after download. The positive news is that developers plan to update [product_name] in the next version to either show an error or ignore trailing spaces. The documentation will also be improved to alert users to avoid extra spaces when entering credentials. I'd like to acknowledge the [company_name] support team for their dedication in helping resolve this issue. Much appreciated. Thank you [user_name], [user_name], [user_name], [user_name], and [user_name].

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue discovered is insufficient error messaging and lack of clear guidance when using [product_name] for cloud downloads with AWS credentials. If extraneous spaces are included from CSV exports, the application does not provide feedback, which can leave users confused about integration failures. Current documentation also lacks warnings related to this formatting problem.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect improved error messages, input validation, and documentation that explicitly cover formatting concerns—such as accidental whitespace—when entering AWS credentials into [product_name] to help avoid easily preventable errors.
